results.summary_before: This design implements a USB to Serial bridge using the USB CDC protocol, allowing a computer to communicate with the chip as a virtual serial port. It uses a 48 MHz clock and connects to USB D+ and D- pins, requiring a 1.5k ohm pull-up resistor on D+ for device detection. Data received from the USB host appears on the rx output pins, and data can be transmitted by setting the tx input pins and asserting tx_valid. A silicon test report confirms both RX and TX work as expected, and the design is based on an open-source USB serial core.
